title: FINS—A Global Occurrence Dataset of Fossil Neoselachians From the Cretaceous to the Quaternary
content:
ABSTRACT

Motivation

Modern sharks, rays and skates (Neoselachii) are a diverse, globally distributed and ecologically important group. They possess a rich, geologically extensive and well-documented fossil record that provides a powerful basis for studying their macroevolution, paleoecology and biogeography. However, addressing paleobiological questions requires quantifying the fossil record through occurrences, that is, records of the presence of a taxon from a unique location in space and time. Although the Paleobiology Database (PBDB) offers an invaluable source of fossil occurrences, it still does not provide a complete compilation of neoselachian data. To facilitate exploring questions in quantitative paleobiology, here we present the Fossil Neoselachians (FINS) dataset—a comprehensive, systematically curated global synthesis of fossil occurrences spanning the past 145 million years.

Main Types of Variables Contained

FINS consists of fossil occurrences, each linked to a collection (location where fossils were reported from) and a source (citation of the publication from which data were obtained). Occurrence data mostly consist of taxonomic variables (e.g., classification, names and ranks) and status (extinct/extant). Collection data provide geographic (e.g., country, ocean and palaeo-coordinates) and geological (e.g., formation and age) variables. All data were subjected to a transparent curation process, which is described through taxonomic and age validation variables.

Spatial Location and Grain

Global, with fossil occurrences recovered from all continents.

Time Period and Grain

From the Cretaceous to the Quaternary (145–0 Ma), with temporal resolution generally corresponding to geological stages or epochs.

Major Taxa and Level of Measurement

Neoselachians (superorders: Selachimorpha and Batoidea). FINS comprises 30,047 occurrences from 5867 collections and 2055 references. It consists of 1621 species, 513 genera, 89 families and 15 orders. Over 70% of occurrences are identified at the species level. Overall, FINS effectively doubles the number of neoselachian records previously available in the PBDB and substantially expands their geographic coverage, particularly in the Global South.

Software Format

The dataset is provided as three .csv files: collections, occurrences and references. It is accompanied by a Shiny Application (FINS app: https://fins-app.shinyapps.io/FINS_App/) to facilitate its visualisation, exploration and expansion.
